name: Lichterfelde electric railway
description: Siemens und Halske’s electrically operated Lichterfelde railway brought electric traction into a local tramway service.

date.basis: The cited account dates this scoped episode.

events.statement: Werner von Siemens reported that the Lichterfelde electric trolley had been officially tested and approved.
events.caveats: A translated excerpt was inspected, rather than the original manuscript; approval differs from public opening.

evidence.locator: Letter to Wiedemann, 12 May 1881, translated excerpt
evidence.supports: Contemporary letter excerpt reports official test and approval.

contributions.resource: Set the speed limit reported in Siemens’s letter

evidence.locator: Letter to Wiedemann, 12 May 1881, translated excerpt
evidence.supports: Siemens states inspectors permitted 20 km/h; the letter also says the trolley was officially tested and approved.

date.basis: The cited account dates this scoped episode.

events.statement: Siemens und Halske opened its Lichterfelde electric railway.
events.caveats: Precise terms of service and fare are not established by this short museum account. A Siemens company history instead dates operation to 12 May; the difference remains unresolved.

unresolved.note: The museum says 16 May opening; the Siemens history says operation began 12 May. The contemporary letter documents testing and approval on 12 May but does not resolve the public-service date.
